name: University of Pisa
header:
University of Pisa
Italy · Laurea Magistrale in Mathematics (MSc); PhD in Mathematics
Curated European option, distinct from Scuola Normale Superiore admission.
Eligibility and preparation · Deadlines by stage · English and GRE · Academic records · Recommendation letters · Written
materials · Funding and fees · Conflicts and remaining checks · Faculty · Sources
Pay attention to
• 2027-2028 academic-year admissions dates were not verified; detailed dated procedures are explicitly the
2026-2027 prior cycle and must not be copied into a 2027 calendar as confirmed.
• Pisa MSc is an Italian-language route for a non-EU applicant abroad. UChicago's English-medium degree does
not establish Italian B2, and US F-1 status does not confer EU-resident admission status.
• Pisa PhD requires a second-cycle-equivalent qualification; a UChicago bachelor's is not automatically
sufficient. SNS and SISSA publish separate equivalency rules and must not be conflated with Pisa's rules.
• General mathematical PhD selection and individual funded-project selections can require separate
applications and tailored motivation/CV material. A project supervisor being named in a 2026 call does not
establish a 2027 position.
• DSU cash amounts depend on income and housing status; accommodation/meals are valued services, not
extra cash. Foreign-income documentation and paper mailing deadlines are substantial prerequisites.
• INdAM's official 2026 scholarship announcement was read, but the linked full call could not be retrieved;
exact amount, citizenship restrictions, letter mechanics and scholarship prompts remain unverified.
• Pardini is an affiliate on the current group roster; Sala's 2026-2027 sabbatical affects contact timing;
Pearlstein's historical US affiliations must not be confused with current Pisa availability.
• Caboara has a verified current roster/profile but the latest relevant paper located was 2022. This does not
meet a strict 2024-2026 recent-paper target; retain the explicit gap.
• Public general admissions pages do not expose all referee invitation, receipt, update or reuse mechanics.
These entries are marked unknown instead of assuming another university's portal behavior.
• All faculty listed are research matches for investigation, not confirmations of willingness or capacity to accept
a student.

sections.title: Eligibility and preparation
sections.text:
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
MSc: a UChicago mathematics BA is a plausible qualifying foreign bachelor's, subject to suitability and
preparation assessment by the degree council. Mathematics curriculum/foreign equivalence is checked;
alternative Italian routes require ≥30 ECTS in mathematics. The Italian-taught route requires non-EU visa
applicants to demonstrate Italian B2. PhD: the legal call requires an Italian master's or a foreign degree
assessed as equivalent to an Italian second-cycle degree, considering level, duration, content and
home-country academic rights. A four-year US BA is not automatically eligible; unlike SNS/SISSA's explicit
four-year language, Pisa's call requires second-cycle equivalence, so plan the MSc route unless Pisa confirms
otherwise. F-1 does not provide Italian residency authorization. [s1] [s2] [s3] [s4]
Before submission [Standing rule]
MSc non-EU visa route: initiate Universitaly pre-enrollment; register in Alice with passport/photo, then use
AmmissioneLM (do not choose the MSc inside Alice), matching the exact program on Universitaly. Obtain
degree, all-course transcript and university-certified syllabi with the required Italian translations. Resolve

Italian B2 certificate/test before visa validation. After council review (approximately 2-3 weeks), upload the
admission decision to Universitaly; arrange visa and residence permit. PhD: check foreign second-cycle
equivalence, select each competition separately, prepare signed CV and academic file, two mathematician
referees, any remote-interview form, and PagoPA payment. Contact project supervisors for restricted positions.
[s1] [s2] [s3] [s4] [s5] [s7]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
Contact faculty whose recent work matches your preparation, and advertised project supervisors when
applicable. Prior AG/arithmetic award explicitly names Giulio Bresciani; higher-Teichmüller award Andrea
Tamburelli. General MSc/PhD does not list a prior supervisor agreement as mandatory. Sala is on sabbatical 21
September 2026-20 September 2027; confirm meeting/supervision timing. Pardini appears as affiliate on
current group roster despite an older/full-professor personal CV; clarify current primary-supervision status. SNS
professors are separate appointments, not automatically Pisa supervisors. [s5] [s15] [s16] [s28]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
MSc: Alice identity account → AmmissioneLM academic file → Universitaly validation/visa → final
Alice/AmmissioneLM documents and fees; progress visible in AmmissioneLM. PhD: Alice register/select
individual competition/upload documents/referee details/final confirmation/save receipt/pay fee. Receipt
includes prematricola and upload count. No editing after confirmation; cancellation resets entire procedure.
Check published rankings and waitlist interest instructions yourself; not every notice is emailed. [s2] [s4] [s7] [s8]
Cycle verification [Prior cycle]
No autumn 2027 academic call or funding schedule established as of 5 November 2026. Explicit dates/budgets
here belong to 2026-27 entry and must not be advanced one year. Current faculty/research pages were
checked separately. [s2] [s4] [s5] [s9] [s14]

sections.text:
Academic application [Prior cycle]
Autumn 2027 dates unpublished. PRIOR MSc non-EU Italian-taught open-admission window: 8 July-31
December 2026; visa applicants must start before arrival, and scholarships/language tests close earlier. PRIOR
PhD: 8 June 2026, 13:00 Italian time. Interviews within 22 June-6 July 2026, with detailed calendar separately
published; final rankings by 27 July. Prior PhD ordinary start 1 November 2026. The general site's August Bando
B date is not established as a second mathematics competition. [s2] [s4] [s5] [s6] [s7]
Funding consideration [Prior cycle]
PhD admission and funded-place competition share the academic deadline. Prior MSc INdAM/Pisa scholarship
deadline 5 September 2026; prior DSU online application 7 September 2026, 13:00 Italian time, plus required
foreign financial originals posted by that date (initial postmark counts). First-year non-EU visa applicants'

own earlier deadline. No 2027 dates established. [s4] [s5] [s10] [s12] [s13] [s14]

PRIOR PhD: at least two mathematician contacts/letters, referees upload by 8 June 2026, 23:59 Italian time.
This is later on the same date than the applicant's 13:00 deadline; no extra day. MSc standard entry: no
references listed in the inspected admissions checklist. INdAM additional-reference requirements could not be
verified because the linked legal PDF was inaccessible. [s2] [s5] [s14]

requirement: prior Pisa ITA L2 test sessions 3 June, 7 July, 22 July 2026 at 14:00 CET/CEST; respective

sections.title: English and GRE
sections.text:
English requirement [Standing rule]
MSc mathematics requires English B2 by graduation if not already demonstrated on entry; acceptable evidence
includes the Pisa CLI examination or recognized certificate. This does not replace Italian B2 for the
Italian-taught non-EU visa route. Italian exemption requires approved CLIQ B2 certification or ministerial
exemption; otherwise ITA L2 ≥55/72 plus successful CLI oral interview. PhD inspected call does not mandate
TOEFL/IELTS or publish a numerical English threshold; confirm interview language with coordinator. [s1] [s3] [s4]
[s5]
UChicago English exemption [Unresolved]
No explicit UChicago/US-degree English exemption for the MSc B2 graduation obligation was found: ask
whether English-medium BA evidence is accepted. UChicago study does not waive Italian B2. PhD no
standardized English certificate requirement identified, so no verified UChicago-specific waiver application. [s1]
[s3] [s4]
GRE General; GRE Mathematics [Standing rule]
Neither GRE General nor GRE Mathematics appears in the inspected MSc requirements or PhD mathematics
selection checklist. This establishes no listed requirement; consideration or prohibition of unsolicited scores is
not stated. [s1] [s2] [s4] [s5]

sections.title: Academic records
sections.text:
Transcripts and degree records [Standing rule]
MSc: bachelor's degree, high-school details, complete university examination transcript, and syllabi on
university letterhead/stamped; published non-EU route requires official Italian translations. Final enrollment
additionally requires Declaration of Value with translated/authenticated/apostilled degree or CIMEA
comparability in Italian, plus passport, visa/residence-permit application receipt and language evidence. PhD:
qualification declaration (call Annex 2), foreign degree/equivalence evidence, Diploma Supplement or
complete records across bachelor's AND master's with all grades/final marks, thesis or summary if unfinished,
publications, signed CV and ID. The portal qualification-entry field says enter only the qualifying
master's/equivalent, but the academic attachment must still document the whole university career. [s2] [s4] [s5]
[s8]
Mathematics-course list [Standing rule]
MSc complete examination list/transcript required; PhD complete bachelor's and master's examination records
with grades and final degree results. No independent US-style mathematics-only list/template specified. [s2] [s5]

Course descriptions [Standing rule]
MSc explicitly requires syllabi for foreign examinations on university letterhead or stamped, with official Italian
translation. Do not substitute a self-written list without approval. PhD foreign-equivalence committee may need
additional content evidence; no separate mandatory standardized syllabus packet beyond the specified
qualification file is fixed. [s2] [s4]

sections.text:
Number and type [Standing rule]
PhD: at least two names and email/telephone contacts of mathematics academics/scholars willing to provide
confidential references; they upload letters under emailed instructions. MSc ordinary admission: none listed.
INdAM scholarship reference count unverified. [s2] [s5] [s14]
Scholarship references [Standing rule]
PhD topic-specific and unrestricted selections use the same minimum two-reference instruction, while
motivation paragraphs differ by topic. DSU is financial/merit assessment and does not list academic
recommendation letters. INdAM full legal conditions and any reference requirement remain unresolved. [s5]
[s11] [s13] [s14]
What sends the invitation [Unresolved]
PhD technical guide places referee entry before final confirmation and says referees receive email instructions;
it does not state whether dispatch occurs immediately on saving details or only at final confirmation. Confirm
in Alice and with referees. MSc no standard reference step established. [s5] [s8]
Before versus after submission [Unresolved]
Exclusive post-submission invitation is not publicly established. Submit early and verify actual dispatch; the
same-day 23:59 referee cutoff leaves little margin after applicant 13:00 close. [s5] [s8]
Receipt confirmation [Unresolved]
Alice application receipt includes prematricola and number of applicant files uploaded, which must match the
intended attachments. This is not proof of recommendation receipt; an individual letter status indicator was
not established. MSc AmmissioneLM shows application progress and Alice later holds enrollment certificate. [s2]
[s8]
Updating and reusing letters [Unresolved]
Submitted PhD application cannot be edited; cancellation resets the whole procedure and is discouraged. No
verified guarantee that letters survive cancellation or are reused across selections/cycles. Each selection needs
a separate application/CV; ask office before deleting a submitted record. [s7] [s8]

sections.title: Written materials
sections.text:
Academic CV / resume [Standing rule]
PhD signed CV, accompanied by valid ID copy, uploaded PDF ≤3 MB per file; cover education, professional and
research experience. No global CV page/font/margin limit. Each selection requires its own CV and a tailored
motivation paragraph of at most one page. MSc standard public checklist does not separately request a CV;
portal/committee-specific additions should be checked. [s2] [s5] [s7] [s8]
Statement of purpose [Standing rule]
PhD MATE01_A asks for a brief motivation paragraph inside the CV, maximum one page, explaining why
applying to the mathematics PhD at Pisa (English rendering of Italian prompt; see selection-sheet page 3 for
original wording). Restricted selections ask why applying for that specific topic under its named supervisor.
This is not an additional unrestricted multi-page SOP. MSc no standalone SOP prompt found. [s2] [s5]

Personal / background statement [Standing rule]
No separate personal/background statement listed in the standard MSc or PhD math requirements. DSU
requests financial declarations, not a personal narrative. [s2] [s5] [s13]
Research-interest statement [Standing rule]
PhD interview discusses preparation, research aptitude and interests developed during study; motivation
paragraph should show fit with the chosen selection. No separately prescribed research-interest essay found.
MSc no standalone interest statement listed. [s2] [s5]
Research proposal [Standing rule]
The general PhD platform has a proposal field only where the program requires it; the 2026 mathematics sheet
requests CV/motivation/thesis/records/publications and interview, not a standalone proposal. Do not interpret
the generic guide as a mathematics proposal mandate. MSc none listed. [s2] [s4] [s5] [s7]
Writing sample / thesis / research summary [Standing rule]
PhD applicants are invited to include master's thesis or a summary if the degree is unfinished; no summary
word/page limit published. Upload PDF ≤3 MB per file; no permission to replace with an external link
established. A BA applicant seeking equivalence must ask which undergraduate thesis/research document is
acceptable. MSc no thesis/writing-sample requirement in standard recognition checklist. [s2] [s5] [s8]
Publications list [Standing rule]
PhD invites copies of any publications with the academic dossier; PDF uploads, ≤3 MB per file. No publications
prerequisite or separate list template stated. List works in CV as appropriate but do not replace requested
copies with links without office approval. MSc none listed. [s2] [s5] [s8]
Course-list document [Standing rule]
No separately authored course statement prescribed. MSc syllabus/transcript documentation is explicit and
substantially more detailed than a simple course list; PhD full examination records are required. [s2] [s5]
Scholarship essays [Standing rule]
PhD restricted-selection CV paragraph, maximum one page: explain motivation for AG/arithmetic geometry
under Giulio Bresciani (MATE03_A), higher Teichmüller theory under Andrea Tamburelli (MATE04_A), ergodic
theory under Claudio Bonanno (MATE02_A), or PDE-constrained measures under Adolfo Arroyo Rabasa
(MATE05_A). Each selection has a separate application. DSU requires household/income/assets documentation
and declarations, not an essay. INdAM exact forms/essays unverified due blocked legal call. SNS ordinary
competition is independent. [s5] [s7] [s11] [s13] [s14]
Other short answers / materials [Standing rule]
PhD uploads include qualifying-degree declaration, ID, and VIDEO request for remote unrestricted interview;
restricted interviews were entirely remote. Technical guide permits a document-description field up to 250
characters, PDF ≤3 MB each; attachments editable only before final confirmation. MSc identity/photo,
Universitaly/visa/residence and language documents; CIMEA/DoV process can take months. No general
font/margin rules established. [s2] [s5] [s8]

sections.title: Funding and fees
sections.text:
Amount and coverage [Prior cycle]
PRIOR 2026-27 PhD: €16,243 gross beneficiary amount per year, monthly payments; 11 funded math
positions, four unrestricted and seven topic-specific. Research budget at least 10% of stipend, plus authorized
overseas-research stipend increase of 50% up to 12 months (18 for qualifying joint/cotutelle routes). MSc no
guaranteed stipend. DSU prior standard non-resident annual cash: €3,338 for ISEE ≤€13,500; €2,262 for
€13,500.01-18,000; €1,060 for €18,000.01-27,000, plus two meals/day and accommodation subject to
availability/conditions and tuition relief. Noncash service valuations (€1,760 meals + €3,150 housing) are not
extra cash. INdAM amount not verified; do not assume a national figure. [s4] [s5] [s11] [s13] [s14]

Years of support [Standing rule]
PhD three years, normally 1 November-31 October, with academic progress requirements. MSc generally two
academic years; DSU award annual with new application each year and later economic/merit requirements.
INdAM duration/renewal details require accessible legal call. SNS two-year funded ordinary route requires its
own entrance competition. [s1] [s4] [s11] [s14]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
PhD funded competitions accept suitable foreign degrees and international candidates. DSU explicitly open to
all nationalities, for the first qualification at the relevant level; prior master's holders ineligible for
master's-level DSU. Non-EU family income/assets require originals, Italian translations and prescribed
legalization. UChicago attendance does not determine citizenship, country-of-origin fee category or financial
independence. INdAM citizenship/foreign-degree eligibility remains unverified. [s4] [s11] [s13] [s14]
Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
PhD topic scholarships bind research to the advertised theme; previous receipt, even partial, of an Italian
doctoral scholarship prevents another such award, and other incompatibility rules apply. Gross stipend is not
net pay. DSU prior ordinary thresholds ISEE ≤€27,000 AND ISPE ≤€60,000, plus degree/merit rules; no
concurrent DSU award for a PhD already receiving a doctoral scholarship. Foreign non-resident classification
has exceptions when family lives in Italy or student meets independence criteria. Missing legalized original
financial evidence can cause exclusion. [s4] [s11] [s13]
Extra funding application [Standing rule]
PhD funding is integrated in each selected competition; make separate applications for open/project selections
but one €30 fee per PhD course. DSU separate online Sportello Studente application plus printed receipt/ID and
foreign financial originals by registered post/courier to ARDSU Toscana, Benefits and Financial Assistance
Service, Viale Antonio Gramsci 36, 50132 Florence; envelope marked DB 2026/2027 for prior call, initial
postmark counts. Tuition reduction: apply in Alice and email ISEEU Parificato to iseeuparificato@unipi.it. INdAM
separate application; SNS separate competition. [s4] [s7] [s10] [s13] [s14]
Other funding routes [Unresolved]
MSc: prior INdAM national competition offered 12 awards, with six additional Pisa awards for nationally eligible
nonwinners enrolling at Pisa, three preferentially for women. Exact amount, citizenship/degree eligibility,
reference/essay rules remain unverified because full INdAM PDF repeatedly failed retrieval. DSU and SNS are
separate alternatives with compatibility conditions. PhD: project scholarships and authorized research-travel
budget/increase; funded doctoral students cannot add DSU doctoral scholarship. Do not assume awards can be
combined. [s4] [s11] [s14]
Application fee [Prior cycle]
PRIOR PhD application fee €30 per doctoral course via PagoPA, one payment covers multiple math selections,
due closing date 23:59; generally nonrefundable. MSc separate application fee not established. Prior tuition
maximum €2,900/year, plus regional tax €140 and initial stamp €16; country-of-origin flat rates
€290/€580/€1,160/€2,900 for low/lower-middle/upper-middle/high-income categories. First-year non-EU visa
tuition schedule: regional/stamp by 31 December 2026, then 30% by 1 February 2027, 25% by 1 March, 25%
by 15 April, 20% by 31 May. Italian tests cost €35 written + €35 oral, if needed. CIMEA/translation/visa costs
separate; 2027-28 amounts unknown. [s3] [s4] [s7] [s9] [s10]
Fee waiver [Standing rule]
PhD application-fee waiver not stated in inspected call; do not confuse tuition exemptions with the €30
competition charge. MSc tuition reductions automatically by country category or through ISEEU Parificato (Alice
request + certificate email), prior visa-entry deadline 31 December 2026. DSU eligible awards include fee
relief; admission can use DSU application receipt in place of initial payment pending assessment. Foreign prior
degrees do not qualify for the published merit-based tuition reduction. [s2] [s4] [s10] [s11]

sections.title: Potential advisers and recent research
sections.text:
1 · Algebraic/arithmetic geometry
Giulio Bresciani
Anabelian geometry, fundamental groups of varieties and stacks, fields of moduli, arithmetic of rational points.
[s17] [s16]
Current Pisa researcher and named supervisor of the prior-cycle funded algebraic/arithmetic geometry PhD project.
Research evidence: 2025 · On the section conjecture over fields of finite type
Official university publication list; the repository handle did not load in the research browser.
Andrea Di Lorenzo
Moduli stacks, integral Chow/Picard groups, intersection theory and cohomological invariants; moduli of curves
and polarized K3 surfaces. [s18] [s16] [s42]
Current Pisa geometry researcher.
Research evidence: 2026 · Polarized twisted conics and moduli of stable curves of genus two
Recent coauthored paper verified in the official SNS research repository; Pisa profile independently establishes current
appointment.
Mattia Talpo
Logarithmic algebraic geometry, stacks, degenerations, tropical geometry and homotopy-theoretic invariants
of log schemes. [s19] [s16]
Current Pisa associate professor.
Research evidence: 2025 · On the profinite homotopy type of log schemes
Official personal publication list identifies Advances in Mathematics 460 (2025), 110018; coauthors Carchedi, Scherotzke and
Sibilla.
Marco Franciosi
Algebraic curves and surfaces, canonical rings, Gorenstein curves and stable-surface/KSBA moduli. [s20] [s16]
Current Pisa associate professor.
Research evidence: 2026 · 2-Gorenstein stable surfaces with K_X^2 = 1 and chi(X)=3
Official university publication list and repository record; recent work also includes half-canonical rings of Gorenstein spin curves

of genus two.
Gregory James Pearlstein
Hodge theory, mixed period maps, degenerations, rigidity and relations with moduli of algebraic surfaces. [s21]
[s16]
Current Pisa associate professor since July 2021; profile also records Texas A&M employment 2013-2024 and Michigan State
2006-2013. Do not treat those historical appointments as current availability.
Research evidence: 2024 · Deformations and rigidity for mixed period maps
Official university publication list, with Chris Peters; also lists 2024 work on unimodal singularities and boundary divisors in KSBA
moduli.
1 · Algebraic/arithmetic geometry - affiliate
Rita Pardini
Algebraic surfaces, abelian covers, irregular varieties and compactifications/moduli of stable surfaces. [s22]
[s16]
Listed as an affiliate on the current Pisa geometry-group roster; personal CV says full professor from 2004 but is not sufficient to
establish current primary-supervision eligibility. Ask about active supervision or co-supervision.
Research evidence: 2025 · On some boundary divisors in the moduli spaces of stable Horikawa surfaces with K^2=2p_g-3
Official personal research page lists preprint arXiv:2502.16322, with Ciliberto.
2 · Number theory/arithmetic geometry
Tamás Szamuely
Arithmetic geometry, Galois and étale cohomology, algebraic cycles, fundamental groups, and
fields/extensions attached to rational points. [s23] [s15]
Current member of Pisa algebra/geometry research community.
Research evidence: 2025 · Cohomology of varieties over the maximal Kummer extension of a number field
Official publication page lists the December 2025 preprint with Davide Lombardo.
Davide Lombardo
Galois representations attached to abelian varieties, Mumford-Tate and Sato-Tate questions, Kummer theory
and computational arithmetic geometry. [s24] [s15] [s23]
Current Pisa associate professor.
Research evidence: 2025 · Cohomology of varieties over the maximal Kummer extension of a number field
Official personal publications page and coauthor Szamuely's official list provide recent-paper evidence.
Andrea Bandini
Iwasawa theory, Selmer and class groups, arithmetic of function fields and Drinfeld modular/quasi-modular
forms. [s25] [s15]
Current Pisa associate professor.
Research evidence: 2026 · Drinfeld quasi-modular forms of higher level
Official university publication list, with Valentino and de Vries; also lists 2026 work on Z_l[[Z_p^d]] and Iwasawa theory.
2 · Number theory/arithmetic algebra
Ilaria Del Corso
Galois/module-theoretic arithmetic, algebraic number theory, Hopf-Galois and skew-brace structures, and unit
groups of rings. [s26] [s15]

Current Pisa algebra faculty member.
Research evidence: 2026 · On Dedekind Skew Braces
Official university publication list; 2025 work on Fuchs' problem also documents the ring/group-theoretic direction.
3 · Representation theory/geometric representation theory
Andrea Maffei
Geometric representation theory, Lie-theoretic geometry, quiver varieties, opers, Weyl modules and
Feigin-Frenkel/critical-level structures. [s27] [s15]
Current Pisa algebra faculty member.
Research evidence: 2024 · The semi-infinite cohomology of Weyl modules with two singular points
Official university publication list, with Fortuna, Lombardo and Melani.
Francesco Sala
Cohomological, K-theoretic and categorified Hall algebras; quantum groups/Yangians; moduli of sheaves and
geometric representation theory. [s28] [s15] [s41]
Pisa associate professor; visiting scientist at Kavli IPMU. Official home page announces sabbatical 21 September 2026-20
September 2027; confirm availability for 2027 advising/contact.
Research evidence: 2026 · Cohomological Hall algebras of one-dimensional sheaves on surfaces and Yangians
Official personal publications page; related 2026 work concerns flops and Hilbert schemes of space-curve singularities.
Leonardo Patimo
Hecke categories, Soergel/Schubert geometry, affine Grassmannians, Demazure operators and
categorical/combinatorial representation theory. [s29] [s15]
Current Pisa algebra researcher.
Research evidence: 2026 · Demazure operators for double cosets
Official university publication list and repository record; 2025 Charges via the Affine Grassmannian further confirms the research
direction.
3 · Representation theory/algebraic combinatorics
Michele D'Adderio
Symmetric and Macdonald polynomials, shuffle theorems, diagonal coinvariant-related algebraic
combinatorics, chromatic functions and representation-theoretic combinatorics. [s30] [s15]
Current Pisa associate professor.
Research evidence: 2025 · Shuffle Theorems and Sandpiles
Official university publication list; also lists Chromatic functions, interval orders and increasing forests (2025).
3 · Representation theory/arrangements
Giovanni Gaiffi
Hyperplane and toric arrangements, wonderful compactifications, their cohomology and associated
algebraic/Lie-theoretic combinatorics. [s31] [s15]
Current Pisa professor and departmental director.
Research evidence: 2025 · An isomorphism between projective models of toric and hyperplane graphic arrangements
Official university publication list.

4 · Complex geometry and holomorphic dynamics
Marco Abate
Complex/Kobayashi geometry, holomorphic iteration, Riemann surfaces and several-complex-variable
dynamics. [s32] [s16]
Current Pisa geometry faculty member.
Research evidence: 2025 · Iterated function systems of holomorphic maps
Official research-paper list, with Ian Short; also lists Parabolic dynamics according to Maurice Heins (2025).
Fabrizio Bianchi
Holomorphic dynamics in several variables, pluripotential theory, currents and measures, entropy and
dynamics on Kähler manifolds. [s33] [s16]
Current Pisa geometry faculty member.
Research evidence: 2026 · On the support of measures of large entropy for automorphisms of Kaehler manifolds
Official research page, with Boymurodov and Rakhimov; also lists Joining rigidity for rational maps and work on Green currents
for Hénon-like maps (2026).
4 · Complex/differential geometry
Diego Conti
Special geometric structures, complex/hypercomplex geometry on Lie groups, pseudo-Kähler and
hypersymplectic metrics, and Einstein-type structures. [s34] [s16]
Current Pisa geometry faculty member.
Research evidence: 2025 · Pseudo-Kähler and hypersymplectic structures on semidirect products
Official university publication list and repository record.
4 · Complex geometry/Teichmüller theory
Andrea Tamburelli
Higher Teichmüller theory and Hitchin components, harmonic/minimal-surface geometry, holomorphic
differentials and related Kähler/symplectic structures. [s35] [s16]
Current Pisa associate professor; named supervisor for two prior-cycle funded positions in higher Teichmüller theory.
Research evidence: 2026 · Limits of cubic differentials and buildings
Official university publication list and repository record, with Loftin and Wolf; 2025 work on a semi-pseudo-Kähler structure on
the SL(3,R) Hitchin component is also listed.
5 · Commutative algebra/algebraic combinatorics - adjacent
Enrico Sbarra
Commutative algebra, local cohomology, Cohen-Macaulay properties, combinatorial commutative algebra and
related algebraic structures. [s36] [s15]
Current permanent Pisa algebra researcher.
Research evidence: 2024 · Zero-divisor graphs and zero-divisor functors
Official university publication list, with Zanardo; sequentially Cohen-Macaulay modules appear in 2022 work.

5 · Computational algebra - recent-paper gap
Massimo Caboara
Computational commutative algebra, Gröbner bases, Hilbert series and Hilbert quasi-polynomials. [s37] [s15]
Current Pisa algebra faculty member. Recent-paper verification gap: the newest relevant paper exposed by the inspected official
list is from 2022; ask about current projects before treating this as a 2027 match.
Research evidence: 2022 · A partial characterization of Hilbert quasi-polynomials in the non-standard case
Latest relevant paper located on the inspected official university publication list; no 2024-2026 paper was verified in this
research pass.
5 · Arrangements and algebraic topology - adjacent
Filippo Gianluca Callegaro
Cohomology of toric/hyperplane arrangements, braid and reflection groups, and combinatorial/topological
structures linked to representation theory. [s38] [s16]
Current Pisa associate professor.
Research evidence: 2024 · Combinatorial generators for the cohomology of toric arrangements
Official university publication list; also lists Cohomology of quasi-abelianized braid groups (2024). A later corrigendum is not used
as the sole recent research paper.
Mario Salvetti
Coxeter, Artin and braid groups, arrangement complements, Milnor fibers and algebraic/combinatorial
topology. [s40] [s16]
Listed on the current Pisa research roster; confirm primary-supervision availability before relying on this contact.
Research evidence: 2024 · Dual structures on Coxeter and Artin groups of rank three
Official university publication list, with Delucchi and Paolini; 2026 conference material was not substituted for a research-paper
record.
5 · Algebraic combinatorics/intersection theory - adjacent
Luis Ferroni
Matroids, Chow rings, intersection cohomology, equivariant Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials and Ehrhart theory.
[s39] [s16]
Current Pisa geometry researcher.
Research evidence: 2025 · Deletion Formulas for Equivariant Kazhdan-Lusztig Polynomials of Matroids
Official university publication list; also lists The Ehrhart polynomial of a matroid specializes to the beta-invariant (2026) and
matroid Chow/intersection-cohomology work (2024).

University of Pisa
Italy · Laurea Magistrale in Mathematics (MSc); PhD in Mathematics
Curated European option, distinct from Scuola Normale Superiore admission.
Eligibility and preparation · Deadlines by stage · English and GRE · Academic records · Recommendation letters · Written
materials · Funding and fees · Conflicts and remaining checks · Faculty · Sources
Pay attention to
• 2027-2028 academic-year admissions dates were not verified; detailed dated procedures are explicitly the
2026-2027 prior cycle and must not be copied into a 2027 calendar as confirmed.
• Pisa MSc is an Italian-language route for a non-EU applicant abroad. UChicago's English-medium degree does
not establish Italian B2, and US F-1 status does not confer EU-resident admission status.
• Pisa PhD requires a second-cycle-equivalent qualification; a UChicago bachelor's is not automatically
sufficient. SNS and SISSA publish separate equivalency rules and must not be conflated with Pisa's rules.
• General mathematical PhD selection and individual funded-project selections can require separate
applications and tailored motivation/CV material. A project supervisor being named in a 2026 call does not
establish a 2027 position.
• DSU cash amounts depend on income and housing status; accommodation/meals are valued services, not
extra cash. Foreign-income documentation and paper mailing deadlines are substantial prerequisites.
• INdAM's official 2026 scholarship announcement was read, but the linked full call could not be retrieved;
exact amount, citizenship restrictions, letter mechanics and scholarship prompts remain unverified.
• Pardini is an affiliate on the current group roster; Sala's 2026-2027 sabbatical affects contact timing;
Pearlstein's historical US affiliations must not be confused with current Pisa availability.
• Caboara has a verified current roster/profile but the latest relevant paper located was 2022. This does not
meet a strict 2024-2026 recent-paper target; retain the explicit gap.
• Public general admissions pages do not expose all referee invitation, receipt, update or reuse mechanics.
These entries are marked unknown instead of assuming another university's portal behavior.
• All faculty listed are research matches for investigation, not confirmations of willingness or capacity to accept
a student.
Eligibility and preparation
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
MSc: a UChicago mathematics BA is a plausible qualifying foreign bachelor's, subject to suitability and
preparation assessment by the degree council. Mathematics curriculum/foreign equivalence is checked;
alternative Italian routes require ≥30 ECTS in mathematics. The Italian-taught route requires non-EU visa
applicants to demonstrate Italian B2. PhD: the legal call requires an Italian master's or a foreign degree
assessed as equivalent to an Italian second-cycle degree, considering level, duration, content and
home-country academic rights. A four-year US BA is not automatically eligible; unlike SNS/SISSA's explicit
four-year language, Pisa's call requires second-cycle equivalence, so plan the MSc route unless Pisa confirms
otherwise. F-1 does not provide Italian residency authorization. [s1] [s2] [s3] [s4]

degree, all-course transcript and university-certified syllabi with the required Italian translations. Resolve

University of Pisa
Italy · Laurea Magistrale in Mathematics (MSc); PhD in Mathematics
Curated European option, distinct from Scuola Normale Superiore admission.
Eligibility and preparation · Deadlines by stage · English and GRE · Academic records · Recommendation letters · Written
materials · Funding and fees · Conflicts and remaining checks · Faculty · Sources
Pay attention to
• 2027-2028 academic-year admissions dates were not verified; detailed dated procedures are explicitly the
2026-2027 prior cycle and must not be copied into a 2027 calendar as confirmed.
• Pisa MSc is an Italian-language route for a non-EU applicant abroad. UChicago's English-medium degree does
not establish Italian B2, and US F-1 status does not confer EU-resident admission status.
• Pisa PhD requires a second-cycle-equivalent qualification; a UChicago bachelor's is not automatically
sufficient. SNS and SISSA publish separate equivalency rules and must not be conflated with Pisa's rules.
• General mathematical PhD selection and individual funded-project selections can require separate
applications and tailored motivation/CV material. A project supervisor being named in a 2026 call does not
establish a 2027 position.
• DSU cash amounts depend on income and housing status; accommodation/meals are valued services, not
extra cash. Foreign-income documentation and paper mailing deadlines are substantial prerequisites.
• INdAM's official 2026 scholarship announcement was read, but the linked full call could not be retrieved;
exact amount, citizenship restrictions, letter mechanics and scholarship prompts remain unverified.
• Pardini is an affiliate on the current group roster; Sala's 2026-2027 sabbatical affects contact timing;
Pearlstein's historical US affiliations must not be confused with current Pisa availability.
• Caboara has a verified current roster/profile but the latest relevant paper located was 2022. This does not
meet a strict 2024-2026 recent-paper target; retain the explicit gap.
• Public general admissions pages do not expose all referee invitation, receipt, update or reuse mechanics.
These entries are marked unknown instead of assuming another university's portal behavior.
• All faculty listed are research matches for investigation, not confirmations of willingness or capacity to accept
a student.
Eligibility and preparation
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
MSc: a UChicago mathematics BA is a plausible qualifying foreign bachelor's, subject to suitability and
preparation assessment by the degree council. Mathematics curriculum/foreign equivalence is checked;
alternative Italian routes require ≥30 ECTS in mathematics. The Italian-taught route requires non-EU visa
applicants to demonstrate Italian B2. PhD: the legal call requires an Italian master's or a foreign degree
assessed as equivalent to an Italian second-cycle degree, considering level, duration, content and
home-country academic rights. A four-year US BA is not automatically eligible; unlike SNS/SISSA's explicit
four-year language, Pisa's call requires second-cycle equivalence, so plan the MSc route unless Pisa confirms
otherwise. F-1 does not provide Italian residency authorization. [s1] [s2] [s3] [s4]
Before submission [Standing rule]
MSc non-EU visa route: initiate Universitaly pre-enrollment; register in Alice with passport/photo, then use
AmmissioneLM (do not choose the MSc inside Alice), matching the exact program on Universitaly. Obtain
degree, all-course transcript and university-certified syllabi with the required Italian translations. Resolve

Italian B2 certificate/test before visa validation. After council review (approximately 2-3 weeks), upload the
admission decision to Universitaly; arrange visa and residence permit. PhD: check foreign second-cycle
equivalence, select each competition separately, prepare signed CV and academic file, two mathematician
referees, any remote-interview form, and PagoPA payment. Contact project supervisors for restricted positions.
[s1] [s2] [s3] [s4] [s5] [s7]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
Contact faculty whose recent work matches your preparation, and advertised project supervisors when
applicable. Prior AG/arithmetic award explicitly names Giulio Bresciani; higher-Teichmüller award Andrea
Tamburelli. General MSc/PhD does not list a prior supervisor agreement as mandatory. Sala is on sabbatical 21
September 2026-20 September 2027; confirm meeting/supervision timing. Pardini appears as affiliate on
current group roster despite an older/full-professor personal CV; clarify current primary-supervision status. SNS
professors are separate appointments, not automatically Pisa supervisors. [s5] [s15] [s16] [s28]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
MSc: Alice identity account → AmmissioneLM academic file → Universitaly validation/visa → final
Alice/AmmissioneLM documents and fees; progress visible in AmmissioneLM. PhD: Alice register/select
individual competition/upload documents/referee details/final confirmation/save receipt/pay fee. Receipt
includes prematricola and upload count. No editing after confirmation; cancellation resets entire procedure.
Check published rankings and waitlist interest instructions yourself; not every notice is emailed. [s2] [s4] [s7] [s8]
Cycle verification [Prior cycle]
No autumn 2027 academic call or funding schedule established as of 5 November 2026. Explicit dates/budgets
here belong to 2026-27 entry and must not be advanced one year. Current faculty/research pages were
checked separately. [s2] [s4] [s5] [s9] [s14]
Deadlines by stage
Academic application [Prior cycle]
Autumn 2027 dates unpublished. PRIOR MSc non-EU Italian-taught open-admission window: 8 July-31
December 2026; visa applicants must start before arrival, and scholarships/language tests close earlier. PRIOR
PhD: 8 June 2026, 13:00 Italian time. Interviews within 22 June-6 July 2026, with detailed calendar separately
published; final rankings by 27 July. Prior PhD ordinary start 1 November 2026. The general site's August Bando
B date is not established as a second mathematics competition. [s2] [s4] [s5] [s6] [s7]
Funding consideration [Prior cycle]
PhD admission and funded-place competition share the academic deadline. Prior MSc INdAM/Pisa scholarship
deadline 5 September 2026; prior DSU online application 7 September 2026, 13:00 Italian time, plus required
foreign financial originals posted by that date (initial postmark counts). First-year non-EU visa applicants'
tuition-reduction application deadline 31 December 2026. SNS's separate funded ordinary competition has its
own earlier deadline. No 2027 dates established. [s4] [s5] [s10] [s12] [s13] [s14]
Reference receipt [Prior cycle]
PRIOR PhD: at least two mathematician contacts/letters, referees upload by 8 June 2026, 23:59 Italian time.
This is later on the same date than the applicant's 13:00 deadline; no extra day. MSc standard entry: no
references listed in the inspected admissions checklist. INdAM additional-reference requirements could not be
verified because the linked legal PDF was inaccessible. [s2] [s5] [s14]
Test-score receipt [Prior cycle]
MSc English B2 may be completed by graduation, not necessarily entry. Italian B2 is a visa/admission
requirement: prior Pisa ITA L2 test sessions 3 June, 7 July, 22 July 2026 at 14:00 CET/CEST; respective
registration/payment deadlines 18 May, 19 June, 14 July at 23:59; then a separate oral test. No 2027 test
calendar established. PhD call lists no GRE or standardized-English score deadline. [s1] [s3] [s4] [s5]

Supporting documents [Prior cycle]
PhD foreign-equivalence evidence and dossier due with application by 13:00; letters and fee by 23:59 same
closing date. Prior qualifying degree by 31 October 2026; admitted foreign-degree holder's original
qualification by 30 November 2026, subject to stated visa exceptions. MSc final documentation/enrollment
within published window; review does not begin with an incomplete file. DSU foreign household originals plus
printed application receipt and ID must be dispatched by scholarship deadline, not merely uploaded later. [s2]
[s4] [s5] [s13]
Accepting an offer [Prior cycle]
PRIOR PhD winners must enroll by 30 July 2026, 13:00 Italian time. Waitlisted candidates must explicitly
register continued interest; roll-down offers published 1/7/14 September require enrollment by 3/10/17
September 2026 at 13:00 respectively. No individual reminder is guaranteed. Later roll-down through 31
December only for unrestricted scholarships; topic positions may be reallocated via November notice restricted
to already-qualified candidates. MSc non-EU first installment/finalization by 31 December 2026; individual
offer/visa conditions may require earlier action. 2027 dates unknown. [s2] [s4] [s9]
English and GRE
English requirement [Standing rule]
MSc mathematics requires English B2 by graduation if not already demonstrated on entry; acceptable evidence
includes the Pisa CLI examination or recognized certificate. This does not replace Italian B2 for the
Italian-taught non-EU visa route. Italian exemption requires approved CLIQ B2 certification or ministerial
exemption; otherwise ITA L2 ≥55/72 plus successful CLI oral interview. PhD inspected call does not mandate
TOEFL/IELTS or publish a numerical English threshold; confirm interview language with coordinator. [s1] [s3] [s4]
[s5]
UChicago English exemption [Unresolved]
No explicit UChicago/US-degree English exemption for the MSc B2 graduation obligation was found: ask
whether English-medium BA evidence is accepted. UChicago study does not waive Italian B2. PhD no
standardized English certificate requirement identified, so no verified UChicago-specific waiver application. [s1]
[s3] [s4]
GRE General; GRE Mathematics [Standing rule]
Neither GRE General nor GRE Mathematics appears in the inspected MSc requirements or PhD mathematics
selection checklist. This establishes no listed requirement; consideration or prohibition of unsolicited scores is
not stated. [s1] [s2] [s4] [s5]
Academic records
Transcripts and degree records [Standing rule]
MSc: bachelor's degree, high-school details, complete university examination transcript, and syllabi on
university letterhead/stamped; published non-EU route requires official Italian translations. Final enrollment
additionally requires Declaration of Value with translated/authenticated/apostilled degree or CIMEA
comparability in Italian, plus passport, visa/residence-permit application receipt and language evidence. PhD:
qualification declaration (call Annex 2), foreign degree/equivalence evidence, Diploma Supplement or
complete records across bachelor's AND master's with all grades/final marks, thesis or summary if unfinished,
publications, signed CV and ID. The portal qualification-entry field says enter only the qualifying
master's/equivalent, but the academic attachment must still document the whole university career. [s2] [s4] [s5]
[s8]
Mathematics-course list [Standing rule]
MSc complete examination list/transcript required; PhD complete bachelor's and master's examination records
with grades and final degree results. No independent US-style mathematics-only list/template specified. [s2] [s5]

Course descriptions [Standing rule]
MSc explicitly requires syllabi for foreign examinations on university letterhead or stamped, with official Italian
translation. Do not substitute a self-written list without approval. PhD foreign-equivalence committee may need
additional content evidence; no separate mandatory standardized syllabus packet beyond the specified
qualification file is fixed. [s2] [s4]
Recommendation letters
Number and type [Standing rule]
PhD: at least two names and email/telephone contacts of mathematics academics/scholars willing to provide
confidential references; they upload letters under emailed instructions. MSc ordinary admission: none listed.
INdAM scholarship reference count unverified. [s2] [s5] [s14]
Scholarship references [Standing rule]
PhD topic-specific and unrestricted selections use the same minimum two-reference instruction, while
motivation paragraphs differ by topic. DSU is financial/merit assessment and does not list academic
recommendation letters. INdAM full legal conditions and any reference requirement remain unresolved. [s5]

What sends the invitation [Unresolved]
PhD technical guide places referee entry before final confirmation and says referees receive email instructions;
it does not state whether dispatch occurs immediately on saving details or only at final confirmation. Confirm
in Alice and with referees. MSc no standard reference step established. [s5] [s8]
Before versus after submission [Unresolved]
Exclusive post-submission invitation is not publicly established. Submit early and verify actual dispatch; the

Receipt confirmation [Unresolved]
Alice application receipt includes prematricola and number of applicant files uploaded, which must match the
intended attachments. This is not proof of recommendation receipt; an individual letter status indicator was
not established. MSc AmmissioneLM shows application progress and Alice later holds enrollment certificate. [s2]
[s8]
Updating and reusing letters [Unresolved]
Submitted PhD application cannot be edited; cancellation resets the whole procedure and is discouraged. No
